content:
The Percentages chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Percentages tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Percentages

Questions on percentage change, successive percentage change, product-constancy (price–consumption) and applications in profit-loss, data interpretation and growth.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • x% of N = (x/100)·N; A as % of B = (A/B)·100.
  • Successive changes a% then b% give a net a + b + ab/100 %.
  • A 20% rise then a 20% fall is a net 4% loss, not 0%.
  • If price rises x%, consumption must fall x/(100+x)·100 % to keep spend constant.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding percentages taken on different bases.
  • Assuming +x% then −x% cancels out.
  • Confusing "x% more than" with "x% less than".

faq.q: Why is percentage so important for CAT?
faq.a: It is the base for Profit & Loss, Interest, Mixtures and a lot of Data Interpretation, so speed here pays off across the whole Quant + DILR section.

faq.q: What are the must-know fraction-to-percent values?
faq.a: 1/2=50%, 1/3=33.33%, 1/4=25%, 1/8=12.5%, 1/9=11.11%, 1/11=9.09% — memorise these for instant mental calculation.
